A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LVBench and contain readable text, tables and figures supporting comparison. v1 includes Appendices A–B; v2 ends with references and contains neither appendix. These are identifiable omissions rather than extraction gaps.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original model evaluations, human accuracy, answer-distribution analyses, filtering ablations and duration analyses. Appendix B also reports dataset composition.

after.justification: Section 4 retains original empirical results and adds evaluations of seven models, alongside human comparisons and diagnostic analyses.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction procedure is unchanged: video screening, six capability categories, human-written multiple-choice questions and joint GLM-4/GPT-4 filtering remain the same. Neither version proposes a new video-understanding model.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 103 videos and 1,549 questions, covering six video categories and six capabilities, with an average duration of 4,101 seconds. LongVideoBench and Video-MME are added to contextual comparisons in Table 1, not used as additional evaluation datasets.

E2.justification: Table 2 expands from eight to fifteen models, adding Video-ChatGPT, LLaVA-OneVision, CogVLM2-Video, GLM4V-Plus, InternVL2-40B, Kangaroo and Qwen2-VL-72B. Table 3 replaces LLaVA-NeXT and Gemini 1.5 Pro with InternVL2-40B and Qwen2-VL-72B. Figures 4–5 also revise their comparator subsets.

E3.justification: v1 specifies model-specific frame counts, including 10 for GPT-4o; v2 gives only generic examples of 32 or 96 frames. Consequently, whether input budgets changed, particularly for GPT-4o's revised results, cannot be established. Native-model sampling at one frame per second, question prompts, answer extraction and duration bins remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The existing diagnostic questions remain, but their evidence changes: Figure 4 adds LWM and substitutes InternVL2-40B for LLaVA-NeXT, while Figure 5 replaces LLaMA-VID, LWM and TimeChat with GLM4V-Plus, InternVL2-40B and Qwen2-VL-72B. Appendix B's analysis of 26 capability combinations is removed. Table 4's filtering ablation is unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds seven result rows and changes the leading reported model from Gemini 1.5 Pro at 33.1% to Qwen2-VL-72B at 41.3%. GPT-4o's reported overall score changes from 27.0% to 34.7%, with input-budget comparability unresolved. Table 3 replaces model-specific category results, and Figures 4–5 revise diagnostic results. Human accuracy remains 94.4%. v2 inconsistently reports InternVL2-40B's overall score as 39.8% in Table 2 and 39.5% in Table 3.

T1.justification: Neither version contains mathematical theory, theorems or proofs. The descriptive task definitions and long-video duration criterion remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows the claimed average-duration advantage over the longest existing dataset from approximately fivefold to fourfold. The central contributions—an unusually long-video benchmark, combinable capabilities and careful annotation—and the conclusion that models remain below human performance are retained.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 removes the suggested explanation linking category-dependent performance to training-data distributions and model architectures. Removing Appendix A also removes qualifications about annotator bias and uncertain long-term availability of source videos. The audio-exclusion limitation and principal language-modeling explanations remain.

D1.justification: Deleting the datasheet removes the JSONL field schema, annotation platform and compensation, collection dates, licensing, hosting, archived-video access conditions and maintenance information. Section 4.1 loses exact model-specific frame counts, and Table 2 removes throughput limits while newly documenting LLM backbones and sizes. The project URL remains; the PDFs establish lost documentation, not withdrawal of the resources themselves.

R1.justification: Section 2 and Table 1 add LongVideoBench and Video-MME to the benchmark context, and references are added for newly evaluated models. The discussion shifts emphasis from CinePile toward longer-video benchmarks, although CinePile remains in Table 1. The fundamental positioning around substantially longer videos is unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 removes both substantive appendices and the acknowledgments, so references now follow the discussion directly. It also revises experimental narratives, adds an explanation of clue duration, changes author information and adopts author–year citations. The main benchmark-construction exposition remains largely unchanged, but the overall document structure is substantially reduced.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 5 are redrawn with revised model selections and scales; Figure 4 changes from four to five pie charts; Figure 6 disappears. Table 1 gains benchmark rows, and Table 2 expands substantially and replaces its Throughput column with LLM. A different document template changes title treatment, headings, headers and text flow. Figures 2–3 retain identical image content.

improvement.justification: The expanded model comparison strengthens evidence that LVBench remains challenging even for the better-performing evaluated systems, and backbone identification improves interpretability. However, v2 removes substantial dataset-reuse documentation and precise input budgets, drops the capability-combination analysis, and introduces the unexplained 39.8% versus 39.5% InternVL2-40B discrepancy. These gains in empirical breadth coexist with material losses in reproducibility and consistency, leaving the net quality direction uncertain.
